record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: Can direct measurements of superallowed beta-spectrum shapes provide useful constraints on additional energy-dependent radiative corrections in beta decay, despite historically limited sensitivity of such spectrum-shape measurements compared with integrated decay rates?

evidence.quote: Measurements of the β spectrum shapes of superallowed decays have been few in the past (43) due to the limited sensitivity one may hope to attain compared to integrated decay rates (see below). With the appearance of additional energy-dependent radiative corrections, discussed in Sec. 5.1, such a measurement could be highly valuable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the theory of nuclear beta decay, a superallowed 0^+ → 0^+ Fermi transition has a differential decay rate (spectrum shape) of the schematic form

  dΓ/dE = G_V^2 |M_F|^2 F(Z,E) p E (E_0 − E)^2 [1 + δ_R(E,Z) + δ'_R(E) + ...],

where E is the electron total energy, E_0 the endpoint energy, p the electron momentum, F(Z,E) the Fermi function, M_F the Fermi matrix element, and δ_R, δ'_R denote nucleus-dependent and energy-dependent outer/inner radiative corrections. The integrated rate (ft value) determines the product G_V^2 |M_F|^2 up to overall radiative corrections, but is by construction insensitive to the energy dependence inside the bracket.

Problem. Determine whether direct measurements of the differential beta spectrum dΓ/dE for superallowed 0^+ → 0^+ transitions can provide useful, quantitative constraints on the energy-dependent radiative corrections (in particular the shape function inside the bracket beyond the leading allowed shape p E (E_0 − E)^2 F(Z,E)), given the historically limited experimental sensitivity of spectrum-shape measurements relative to integrated ft-value determinations. Specifically, quantify the precision with which the energy dependence of the radiative-correction shape function can be extracted from feasible direct spectrum-shape experiments, and compare it to the precision needed to test current theoretical predictions for these corrections.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open experimental/theoretical question in modern beta-decay physics. Recent reviews and experimental programs (e.g., precision spectrum-shape measurements using cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy, ion traps, and gas-filled detectors) are actively pursuing such measurements, but no definitive demonstration that direct superallowed spectrum-shape measurements yield useful constraints on energy-dependent radiative corrections has been established as of the most recent literature.
